links.outcome: LLM accuracy on COVID-19 and pregnancy clinical knowledge questionnaire
links.effect: ChatGPT-4 and Copilot 97% (32/33), Bard 94% (31/33), ChatGPT-3.5 82% (27/33); ChatGPT-4 incorrectly stated increased miscarriage risk; minor inaccuracies for Bard and Copilot.
links.quote: In terms of LLMs' knowledge, ChatGPT-4 and Microsoft Copilot each scored 97% (32/33), Google Bard 94% (31/33), and ChatGPT-3.5 82% (27/33).

links.outcome: Readability of LLM responses (Flesch-Kincaid grade level and Reading Ease)
links.effect: Copilot most accessible (FKGL 9.9, FRE 49); ChatGPT-4 12.4 and 37.1; ChatGPT-3.5 12.9 and 35.6; Bard 12.9 and 35.8, described as particularly complex.
links.quote: Finally, concerning the readability analysis, Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level and Flesch Reading Ease Score showed that Microsoft Copilot was the most accessible at 9.9 and 49, followed by ChatGPT-4 at 12.4 and 37.1, while ChatGPT-3.5 (12.9 and 35.6) and Google Bard (12.9 and 35.8) generated particularly complex responses.

unlisted_practices: Sentiment analysis of LLM responses for neutral and objective tone

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates and compares the knowledge, readability, and sentiment of four LLMs on a validated questionnaire regarding COVID-19 in pregnancy without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
